answer: One concrete mechanism: pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because grove only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. Concretely, inlet is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any lotus approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
